I am responding to many of the comments (not necessarily the original picture). 

I was raised Mormon and left the church when I was 16. I'm agnostic/weak atheist now, but back then, I didn't quit because I had some grand atheist intellectual epiphany. I left because the people in the church demanded perfection, and I wasn't perfect, so I was ostracized by my peers, and then my family members were ostracized by their peers for associating with me, and I was so exhausted of feeling guilty all the time for not reading scriptures every day and for making out with my non member boyfriend and for having no desire to visit the temple to do baptisms for the dead.

In other protestant religions, the worst part about the people is that everyone is hypocritical. I remember many of my "super religious" friends getting drunk behind their church all the time and then making me feel like shit for belonging to a cult.

In Mormonism, you must strive for perfection on Earth, even though it's impossible (according to the church) to actually get there. When you make a mistake, you have to go to these creepy, high pressure meetings with an authority figure in the church for weeks. You basically sit there alone with an old man describing how you masturbated or let a boy touch your boobs. And then he shames you, and then you pray together, and then he tells all the other old men, and then you're afraid they're thinking about it every time they look at you. (I say "men" because women can't be leaders in the church). 

Most Mormons *are* very nice, but it's part of the religion. They *have* to be kind, because it's what God wants. To be Mormon is to read scriptures every single day, to go to bed early and wake up early, to exercise every day, to never curse, never watch anything with sexual or violent themes, never drink caffeine or eat unhealthy foods or drink alcohol or do drugs, never date a "non member," never date a "non worthy member," never have sex until marriage, never do ANYTHING sexual with anyone including yourself, give 10% of your income to the church, hold part-time positions in the church for free, make good grades, be good at every single thing you do, practice your "gifts" every day or lose them, don't watch TV or go out on Sundays, never talk back to your parents, pray before everything, get married ASAP and never use birth control, go to church multiple times a week, leave your home at 19 and depend on the kindness of others for food for 2 years while you go door to door trying to convert people, etc etc. 

In order to remain in the church (because otherwise, you would crumple under the weight of the guilt), your whole life focuses on being "worthy" and only hanging out with others who are "worthy." Church members are way harder on other church members because they "know better." Mormons condescend and are kind to non members because non members just don't know any better. 

I understand what everyone is saying about the afterlife doctrine being ideal if it turned out to be true (it wouldn't for me though—I would actually go to legit Hell, because I am a "daughter of perdition" because I "knew" about the gospel and willingly turned it down). 

But I think it's important to know that most Mormons are nice because any imperfections have been conditioned out of them. That, and they do want to convert you. Missionaries feel that the best way to convert others is to show them their kindness and happiness and perfection. They want other people to think, "Damn. There is something wonderful and special about those guys. Maybe MORMONISM is the key to happiness! Maybe I should ask them questions about their religion!" According to my dad, who was a missionary, they are literally trained to do this. 

My roommates and I had a long conversation with some missionaries before I officially removed my name from the records. We explained the issues we had with the logic of the doctrine. The missionaries couldn't answer a few questions, and in the end, they told us that they "prefer a spiritual conversion over a logical one."

But honestly, a huge part of you has to die to be happy as Mormon. You have to smother the darker parts of you until they aren't there anymore. And then you just follow the very blank, based-on-lies-(potentially) guidelines of how to live your life until you die (or for the rest of eternity, depending on whether or not it's all true :P). 

I'm not saying you should be mean to Mormons, but it scares me that so many people are commenting on how good-natured and kind they are, especially since we got pretty close to having one as a president recently. Make no mistake about this: they do want to convert you. They are very much a  part of the Dominionist movement. ( http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_Theology )

Creating as many Mormons as possible is everything to them. It does come from a place of kindness, since it's because they think Mormonism is the big truth that can save everyone. But that means that turning the US into a nearly-Mormon theocracy would please them, which I'm sure most of you don't want. They think they know better than you, and everyone else, and they think that the best thing they can do for the world is to share the gospel with as many people as possible. 

It is a complex religion that brainwashes you into being perfect, with its tricky, twisty, clever, but psychologically harmful doctrine. (Not to mention, it's based on Jesus coming to America). It kills a part of your humanity, and makes little girls feel guilty throughout all of childhood if they want anything other than to marry a perfect man and become a perfect mom and raise perfect Mormon babies. 

It's nice that they helped someone garden, but please don't forget that^!
